overrides.why_this_special: SGLang v0.5.17 is a material W33 serving release: it combines day-0 support for major new model families with a Rust frontend, session-aware cache behavior, MoE serving paths, and concrete loading/memory optimizations.

claims.text: SGLang published v0.5.17 on 2026-08-08 UTC with day-0 support for Kimi K3 and MiniMax-H3 plus an initial Rust server/frontend path.

The project release notes report session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache behavior, new DeepSeek-V4 serving kernels, MoE prefill/loading improvements, and multiple measured throughput/memory gains.

limitations: Performance and memory numbers in the release notes are project-reported measurements on the stated hardware/configurations and are not independently reproduced in this Evidence pass.
Day-0 support establishes serving integration, not independent validation of the supported models' own capability claims.

Verify chronology, primary-source identi.finding: The GitHub release page directly establishes the W33 release date, the model-support list, Rust-server work, cache changes, and the project-attributed optimization claims. It is distinct from narrower vLLM/FlashInfer releases because it bundles model onboarding, server architecture, cache semantics, and MoE serving changes in one release.

overrides.rationale: Strong Inference / Serving candidate with enough independently identifiable subthemes for a concise release article or systems sidebar.

artifact.canonical_name: Transformers v5.15.0 / Muse Glimmer model addition

overrides.why_this_special: Transformers v5.15.0 landed in W33 and its release notes explicitly surface Meta Muse Glimmer as a newly released multimodal model, providing an independent integration/chronology anchor for the Grok lead.

claims.text: Hugging Face published Transformers v5.15.0 on 2026-08-10 UTC and included Meta Muse Glimmer under New Model additions.
The Hugging Face release notes describe Muse Glimmer as a dense 30B multimodal model with a 2B vision encoder and 28B text decoder and state that it was released that day under Apache 2.0.

limitations: This verifies the Hugging Face project release and its Muse Glimmer integration/release-note record. Grok r3 is retained only as trend-priority evidence; detailed model capability, architecture, and performance claims remain attributed unless separately verified from Meta/model-card sources.

Verify chronology, primary-source identi.finding: Transformers v5.15.0 directly establishes the 2026-08-10 project release and Muse Glimmer model addition. The r3 trend lead survives reconciliation because the model identity is independently corroborated here; detailed model claims remain attributed to the project/Meta source chain.

overrides.rationale: Candidate-level open-weight/model-integration lead; use the Transformers release as the canonical W33 Evidence anchor and use Grok r3 only to prioritize the trend.

overrides.grouping_note: v0.27.0 is the material W33 release and v0.27.1 is an immediate patch-level continuation; grouping avoids double counting one release family.
overrides.why_this_special: vLLM v0.27.0 is a substantial W33 serving release and v0.27.1 follows immediately as a patch release, so the series is one coherent systems candidate.

claims.text: vLLM published v0.27.0 on 2026-08-10 UTC and v0.27.1 on 2026-08-11 UTC.

The v0.27.0 release notes describe a broad set of model-support, engine, quantization, distributed-serving, and platform changes; v0.27.1 is an immediate maintenance continuation rather than an independent feature release.

limitations: The release-note performance and compatibility statements remain project claims unless reproduced under the same model/hardware/configuration.
The series is broad; article treatment should select a small number of technically material changes rather than enumerate the changelog.

Verify chronology, primary-source identi.finding: Both GitHub release pages establish the series chronology inside W33. v0.27.0 is the feature-bearing release and v0.27.1 is the immediate patch continuation, supporting one grouped candidate.

overrides.rationale: Candidate as a major serving/runtime release series; compare against SGLang/FlashInfer at Candidate Selection rather than treating all three as separate lead stories automatically.

overrides.why_this_special: FlashInfer v0.6.17 is a W33 low-level inference-kernel release that complements higher-level SGLang/vLLM changes and is relevant to MoE, attention, and GPU serving performance.

The release notes describe kernel/runtime improvements relevant to attention, MoE expert parallelism, quantized inference, and serving backends.

limitations: Kernel performance claims are implementation- and hardware-specific and are not independently benchmarked in this Evidence pass.
